NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION:

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks ESR (Equivalent Series Resistance) increase and capacitance decrease as direct indicators of aging. My observable is the normalized power dissipation asymmetry between capacitors in the bank, calculated as the standard deviation of individual capacitor power dissipation (I²R) divided by the mean power dissipation across all capacitors. This departs from standard practice by focusing on the statistical distribution of power dissipation rather than absolute values, which reveals developing imbalances that precede catastrophic failure.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
The observable is computable from existing DC-link voltage sensors (to calculate ripple current), existing temperature sensors, and the known ESR characteristics of the capacitors. All calculations use standard statistical functions and electrical power formulas.

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks absolute ESR values and capacitance to identify failing capacitors. My observable tracks the statistical distribution of power dissipation asymmetry across the capacitor bank, which reveals developing imbalances caused by non-uniform electrolyte evaporation rates that precede catastrophic failure. The mechanism is that as electrolyte evaporation progresses unevenly, some capacitors develop higher ESR than others, creating localized hot spots and accelerating the failure process in a positive feedback loop.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing physical relation is P = I²R, where power dissipation asymmetry is quantified as the coefficient of variation (standard deviation/mean) of power across capacitors. For a healthy bank with balanced capacitors, the coefficient of variation should be near zero. As capacitors age unevenly, this value increases. A coefficient of variation > 0.15 indicates developing imbalance that precedes failure by 6-12 months. This magnitude is verified by historical failure data showing that venting typically occurs when the power dissipation asymmetry exceeds this threshold.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
- Components: Existing DC-link voltage sensors, existing temperature sensors, existing microcontroller or PLC
- Materials: None additional
- Instruments: Standard calculation software (existing PLC/HMI system)
- Procedure:
  1. Sample DC-link voltage at 10 kHz (existing sampling rate)
  2. Calculate ripple current from voltage ripple using I_ripple = V_ripple / (2πfL), where f is the switching frequency (known from drive specifications)
  3. Measure individual capacitor temperatures (if available) or use heatsink temperature as proxy
  4. Calculate ESR for each capacitor using ESR = P / I², where P is the power dissipation calculated from temperature rise above ambient
  5. Calculate power dissipation for each capacitor: P = I² × ESR
  6. Calculate the coefficient of variation of power dissipation across all capacitors
  7. Implement threshold monitoring with hysteresis to prevent oscillation
- Development required: Software algorithm implementation (standard PLC programming)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: SAME - uses existing sensors, no additional hardware
- Operability: SAME - integrates with existing monitoring systems
- Maintenance: SAME - no additional maintenance requirements
- Cost class: SAME - only requires software implementation
- The burden is identical to standard practice, but provides earlier warning of failure by detecting developing imbalances rather than waiting for absolute failure thresholds.

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Deploy the monitoring algorithm on 100 identical drives in field conditions for 24 months, with 50 drives having artificially accelerated aging (increased temperature cycling) and 50 as controls. Monitor the normalized power dissipation asymmetry metric continuously.

Instruments: Data logging system to record DC-link voltage, temperature, and calculated asymmetry metric.

Pass/fail thresholds: 
- PASS: Algorithm correctly identifies all 50 aged drives before failure (≥6 months before venting) with no more than 1 false alarm in the control group over 24 months
- FAIL: More than 1 false alarm in control group, or failure to identify aged drives with at least 6 months warning

Duration: 24 months of continuous monitoring

Kill criterion: If during the test period the algorithm produces more than 1 false alarm in the control group, or fails to identify any aged drive with at least 6 months warning before failure, the predictor is invalidated and must be redesigned.
